anchors.statement: sc-lint's setup command must itself run atm-core's setup step (today a Justfile recipe that builds .bootstrap-venv), so atm-core's Justfile no longer has to.
anchors.quote: atm-core can delete its Justfile glue (_py, sc_lint_clippy_prefix, _sc-lint-clippy) because sc-lint runs the setup step and uses the right Python itself.
anchors.scope: The item changes sc-lint setup/provisioning, consumer config ([tool.sc-lint].setup), or the just setup flow.

anchors.statement: sc-lint must itself select the Python interpreter for each atm-core lint and test step that atm-core's Justfile recipes _py, sc_lint_clippy_prefix and _sc-lint-clippy select today.
anchors.quote: atm-core can delete its Justfile glue (_py, sc_lint_clippy_prefix, _sc-lint-clippy) because sc-lint runs the setup step and uses the right Python itself.
anchors.scope: The item changes interpreter selection, runner config ([tool.sc-lint].runner), step argv or step environment in crates/sc-lint.

anchors.statement: sc-lint's dependency ownership check (global_dependency_ownership) must be able to limit enforcement to source files only.
anchors.quote: sc-lint enforces dependency ownership on source files only, and we know which of atm-core's three boundary settings it already covers.
anchors.scope: The item changes global_dependency_ownership or SCB-MANIFEST-004 in crates/sc-lint-boundary, or their config keys.

anchors.statement: PORT-010 must not report a cfg(unix) item that has a same-name #[cfg(not(unix))] sibling in the same scope, whether that scope is a module, an inherent impl, or the crate root.
anchors.quote: S3  cfg(unix) item with a same-name `#[cfg(not(unix))]` sibling in the same scope (module, inherent impl, or crate root). Rows 2, 4, 6, 14, 18. This is #720 generalized beyond crate-root main.rs.
anchors.scope: The item changes PORT-010 sibling detection or port010 fixtures (crate_root_main, module, inherent impl).

anchors.statement: [tool.sc-lint].setup.pre must accept an argv list that the sc-lint setup command (just setup) runs before it provisions sc-lint.
anchors.quote:
`setup.pre` (argv run by `just setup` before sc-lint provisioning)
[…]
[tool.sc-lint.setup]
pre = ["just", "bootstrap"]
[…]
**(c) Commitment:** yes, we commit to this split now and will adopt in the first release that ships it
anchors.scope: The item edits ScLintConfigFile or consumer config parsing, or the just setup / installer flow.

anchors.statement: When runner.python names a venv, sc-lint must prepend that venv's bin directory (Scripts on Windows) to the PATH of every step's child process.
anchors.quote:
(2) the venv's bin/Scripts dir is prepended to the child's PATH (our `python_cmd` does this today so helpers that spawn `python` stay pinned)
[…]
(plus the PATH prepend in (2) applied to every step)
anchors.scope: The item changes step child environment or runner.python handling in crates/sc-lint.

anchors.statement: global_dependency_ownership must offer a config setting that restricts its check to src/**/*.rs, the source-only scope atm-core's checker uses.
anchors.quote:
The released 0.8.2 `global_dependency_ownership` policy has no source-only scope equivalent to the atm-core consumer check.
[…]
The previous atm-core checker passes on this tree because it scans `src/**/*.rs` and does not treat separate integration-test targets as production source. There is no config setting to preserve that source-only scope. atm-core therefore retains this rule locally pending a released source-only scope; no roots or excludes were added to suppress the findings.
anchors.scope: The item changes global_dependency_ownership or SCB-MANIFEST-004 config in crates/sc-lint-boundary.

anchors.statement: Each of atm-core's three [boundaries] keys (manifest_dependency_allowlists, global_dependency_ownership, manifest_section_rules) must be classified as covered or not covered by the latest released sc-lint-boundary.
anchors.quote: atm-core `[boundaries]` config carries manifest_dependency_allowlists, global_dependency_ownership and manifest_section_rules (.just/lint-config.toml). Released sc-lint-boundary has manifest_policy.rs / package_policy.rs (--rule manifests / --rule dependencies, #73). Verify which of the three atm-core keys are covered and file the remainder as config-surface gaps.
anchors.scope: The item audits atm-core [boundaries] keys against sc-lint-boundary or writes a parity table.

anchors.statement: A config-surface gap issue must be filed in randlee/sc-lint for each atm-core [boundaries] key (manifest_dependency_allowlists, global_dependency_ownership, manifest_section_rules) that released sc-lint-boundary does not cover.
anchors.quote: atm-core `[boundaries]` config carries manifest_dependency_allowlists, global_dependency_ownership and manifest_section_rules (.just/lint-config.toml). Released sc-lint-boundary has manifest_policy.rs / package_policy.rs (--rule manifests / --rule dependencies, #73). Verify which of the three atm-core keys are covered and file the remainder as config-surface gaps.
anchors.scope: The item files sc-lint-boundary config-surface gap issues or links them from the parity table.

anchors.statement: With atm-core's PORT-010 path exclusions removed, sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must report no finding on atm-core that the verdict table in sc-lint issue #786 classifies as a false positive or deliberate exception.
anchors.quote:
atm-core can remove its PORT-010 exclusions and get zero false alarms, while real Windows gaps are still reported.
Definition question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "false alarm = a finding #786's table classifies as false positive or deliberate exception" Rand: "yes"
anchors.scope: The item changes PORT-010 in crates/sc-lint-portability, its fixtures or docs, or atm-core PORT-010 exclusions.

anchors.statement: A parity table under docs/plans/phase-m/ must record whether sc-lint covers each of atm-core's boundary settings manifest_dependency_allowlists, global_dependency_ownership and manifest_section_rules.
anchors.quote:
sc-lint enforces dependency ownership on source files only, and we know which of atm-core's three boundary settings it already covers.
Definition question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "we know = written in a parity table in the Phase M docs for manifest_dependency_allowlists, global_dependency_ownership, manifest_section_rules" Rand: "yes"
anchors.scope: The item audits atm-core [boundaries] settings against sc-lint-boundary or writes a parity table in the Phase M docs.

anchors.statement: sc-lint must be able to export the [tool.sc-lint].runner.python venv interpreter as PYO3_PYTHON to native (non-python) steps such as cargo clippy.
anchors.quote:
`runner.python` only rewrites step argv; cargo clippy needs the venv interpreter exported as `PYO3_PYTHON` and the venv dir on PATH for native (non-python) steps.
[…]
We need one more knob, e.g. `runner.export_env = ["PYO3_PYTHON"]` (plus the PATH prepend in (2) applied to every step), or a per-step `env`.
anchors.scope: The item changes step environment, runner config, or clippy steps in crates/sc-lint.

anchors.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must offer an approved exception path through which a consumer knowingly opts a #[cfg(unix)] item out of reporting.
anchors.quote: Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "ANC-015 against ANC-017. ANC-015 says to report any `cfg(unix)` item with no portable counterpart. ANC-017 says to exempt public POSIX-only helpers that have no Windows counterpart. They overlap" Rand (2026-10-30): "we must have an approved exception path to knowingly opt out."
anchors.scope: The item changes PORT-010 exemptions, classification or suppression in crates/sc-lint-portability.

anchors.statement: sc-lint must give a consumer a method to override the interpreter that sc-lint runs sc_lint.* wheel helper steps on.
anchors.quote: Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "GH-198.runner-argv against GH-198.kit-helpers. The literal rule \"a leading `python` becomes the `runner.python` interpreter\" would also rewrite `python -m sc_lint.*`. The kit-helpers record says those always use the kit interpreter, never overridden." Rand (2026-10-30): "a consumer must have a method to override behavior."
anchors.scope: The item changes step argv construction, interpreter selection or runner.python handling in crates/sc-lint.

anchors.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must report every #[cfg(unix)] item that has no #[cfg(windows)], #[cfg(not(unix))] or portable counterpart, unless an approved exception declaration opts it out.
anchors.quote:
atm-core can remove its PORT-010 exclusions and get zero false alarms, while real Windows gaps are still reported.
Definition question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "real Windows gap = a cfg(unix) item with no Windows, cfg(not(unix)) or portable counterpart" Rand: "yes"
Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "ANC-015 against ANC-017. ANC-015 says to report any `cfg(unix)` item with no portable counterpart. ANC-017 says to exempt public POSIX-only helpers that have no Windows counterpart. They overlap" Rand (2026-10-30): "we must have an approved exception path to knowingly opt out."
anchors.scope: The item changes PORT-010 exemptions, classification or suppression in crates/sc-lint-portability.

anchors.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must exempt pub POSIX-only #[cfg(unix)] helpers such as is_owned_by_uid and current_uid in crates/atm-core/src/atm_temp.rs only through an approved exception declaration.
anchors.quote:
S8  (only the pub caveat) pub cfg(unix)-only POSIX helpers (`is_owned_by_uid`, `current_uid` in atm_temp.rs) with no Windows counterpart because the concept does not exist; Windows uses a different check. Row 1. Sc-lint docs say pub items stay checked, so the sc-lint team must choose: exempt (S1 transitively) or keep reporting. Not a parity gap.
Rand ruling (relayed by team-lead 2026-10-30): "S8 = EXEMPT pub POSIX-only helpers"
Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "ANC-015 against ANC-017. ANC-015 says to report any `cfg(unix)` item with no portable counterpart. ANC-017 says to exempt public POSIX-only helpers that have no Windows counterpart. They overlap" Rand (2026-10-30): "we must have an approved exception path to knowingly opt out."
anchors.scope: The item changes PORT-010 handling of pub items, helper exemptions or exception declarations in crates/sc-lint-portability.

anchors.statement: By default, sc-lint must run sc_lint.* wheel helper steps on the sc-lint kit's own venv interpreter (.sc-lint/venv), even when [tool.sc-lint].runner.python is set.
anchors.quote:
plain `python` steps use `runner.python`; `sc_lint.*` wheel helpers always use the kit interpreter and `runner.python` must never apply to them.
Conflict question (team-lead, 2026-10-30): "GH-198.runner-argv against GH-198.kit-helpers. The literal rule \"a leading `python` becomes the `runner.python` interpreter\" would also rewrite `python -m sc_lint.*`. The kit-helpers record says those always use the kit interpreter, never overridden." Rand (2026-10-30): "a consumer must have a method to override behavior."
anchors.scope: The item adds or changes how sc_lint.* helper steps (deny, manifests, shear, spell) are run in crates/sc-lint.

anchors.statement: When [tool.sc-lint].runner.python names a venv, a leading python in any lint or test step argv that does not run an sc_lint.* wheel helper must resolve to that venv's interpreter on every OS.

(1) a leading `"python"` in any lint **or test** step argv resolves to that venv's interpreter on every OS
plain `python` steps use `runner.python`; `sc_lint.*` wheel helpers always use the kit interpreter and `runner.python` must never apply to them.
anchors.scope: The item changes step argv construction or runner.python handling in crates/sc-lint.
